name: Istanbul
hook: One city, three names, two continents — Byzantium, the Bosphorus and the Orient Express.

facts.label: Byzantium
facts.statement: Legend says Byzas founded the city as Byzantium after consulting the Oracle of Delphi; Yeats later imagined "Sailing to Byzantium."

facts.label: Constantinople
facts.statement: It was Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire, before the Turkish Republic made the old name Istanbul official.
Mehmed II's Ottomans took the city in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire; in 1204 the Fourth Crusade had already sacked it.

facts.label: the Bosphorus
facts.statement: The Bosphorus strait separates Istanbul's European and Asian sides; the city straddles both continents and is linked by suspension bridges.

facts.label: Hagia Sophia
facts.statement: Hagia Sophia — the Church of the Divine Wisdom — dates to the 6th century and stands on the site of a cathedral burned in the Nika riot of 532.

facts.label: the Blue Mosque
facts.statement: The Blue Mosque, with its six minarets, was built to rival Hagia Sophia across from it and survived the 1999 earthquake undamaged.

facts.label: the Orient Express
facts.statement: The Orient Express first ran from Paris to Istanbul in 1883; Agatha Christie set her 1934 Poirot novel aboard it, partly written at the Pera Palace.
